purpose: Carteolol eye drops are used to treat high pressure inside the eye, a condition called glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve. It is important to use it regularly even if your eyes feel fine.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes a fluid that can build up and cause pressure. Carteolol works by reducing the amount of this fluid your eye produces, which lowers the pressure inside the eye. Think of it like slowing down a faucet so a sink does not overflow.
common_side_effects: Eye stinging or burning right after putting in the drops, mild eye redness or irritation, blurred vision, and watery eyes. Some people may notice a slightly slower heart rate or feel a bit tired, especially when starting the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have asthma, COPD, a slow heart rate, heart failure, or diabetes, as this medication can affect these conditions. Do not stop using the drops suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any surface to keep it clean and germ-free. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Always wash your hands before using the drops, tilt your head back, gently pull down your lower eyelid, and place one drop inside. Close your eye gently for about one to two minutes after each dose.
